mei: Ran into a parity issue while onboarding a new customer. Their integration hits the REST endpoint fine but our Python SDK raises: "TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'model'".

mei: REST request that works: POST /v1/generations with body {"model":"rdb-gpt-3", "prompt":"hi"} and returns 200.

nina: That sounds like the old SDK still expects "engine" in the client call. We renamed the REST param to "model" last quarter but only partially updated libs.

sam: Confirmed. The python client schema validation uses "engine" in generate() signature. I have a small compatibility patch to accept both names and emit a DeprecationWarning when "engine" is passed.

carlos: Also flag: retry semantics differ. REST gateway has 3 retries with exponential backoff but python client is currently 0 retries. Customer hit occasional 503s. We should harmonize defaults.

mei: For short-term unblock, I added this wrapper in prod: client.generate(**({"engine": params.pop('model')} if 'model' in params else params)). Works.

devex-bot: PR created: python-sdk#589 (compat + retry) — CI queued.

sam: Plan: quick patch release for python SDK, backlog task to sync docs & add integration test for generation path. I'll also add a note about env var names (RW_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_KEY) to the onboarding checklist.

nina: Thanks. If we can get the release out today, we avoid more churn.

mei: I'll coordinate with support and leave a comment in the ticket. End of thread.
